content:
maya: customer report from AcmeCorp - sudden embeddings throughput drop and intermittent 400 errors. They say vectors/sec fell ~4x around 2026-03-10 17:10 UTC. ticket #SUP-4821.

maya: excerpt from customer: "we started getting 400s with message `dimension mismatch` and throughput dropped. Our billing spiked too — charges look higher for the same traffic. Can you help?" :frowning_face:

diego: ok grabbing logs and config. do we have their request body / example? maya can you paste a failing request?

maya: pasted a sanitized repro they provided:

```json
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small-v2","input":["hello world"],"metadata":{"expected_dim":1536}}'
```

maya: their client library adds an extra header `X-Client-Dimensions: 1537` in some code paths. customer says they upgraded their SDK recently.

sarah: pulling runtime metrics for that org and the global GPU pool. quick summary: around 17:09 UTC we see queue_depth jump from avg 20 -> 220 and gpu_util jump 40%->96% on node pool embed-pool-3. vectors/sec (embedding outputs) for that org dropped from ~110k -> ~28k. tokens/sec (text-gen metric) irrelevant for embed endpoint but some dashboards mixed them which confused initial triage. linking grafana panels: https://grafana/redwood/embed/ORG-1234/throughput

infra-bot: alert: embed-pool-3 high gpu_util (>=90%) for 8m, queue_depth >= 200 for 5m.

elias: suspicious: if a client sends inconsistent dimension metadata/headers we have logic that attempts to batch different model shapes by padding to the largest dim in the batch. padding is expensive and can cause kernel fallback to FP32 for certain quantized kernels. i want to see if their requests were being mixed with other orgs or model variants in the same batch.

jim: checking batching config — we rolled a small runtime patch in release r23.4 yesterday that changed batching grouping heuristics to be less strict (to improve tail latency for mixed-model workloads). could be related. r23.4 also changed the default max_batch_size from 256 -> 512 for embeddings.

maya: customer SDK change + our new batching heuristics could be the combo. customer sent a trace:

```
[trace] request 0: model embed-small-v2, dimension header 1537
[trace] request 1: model embed-small-v2, dimension header 1536
[trace] batched into single job -> runtime padded to 1537 -> kernel chosen: quant-fallback-fp32 -> GPU mem + compute spike
```

maya: they also had some clients retrying on 400s which multiplied active concurrent requests during the spike.

diego: repro steps I ran locally (mimics customer):

1) start 6 concurrent requests with dims alternating 1536/1537
2) use batcher config max_batch_size=512 and batching grouping relaxed
3) observe gpu-util and vectors/sec drop

commands I used:

```bash
# quick stress repro
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood.local/v1/embeddings \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"embed-small-v2\",\"input\":[\"sample $i\"],\"meta\":{\"client_dim\":$((1536 + (i%2)))} }" &
done

# monitor
watch -n1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv
```

elias: in the repro I see kernel selection switching from 'q8_opt' to 'fp32_generic' when any padding is applied. that doubles per-token compute and memory, explains both decreased vectors/sec and higher billing for same logical requests (longer GPU time -> more billed units in Dedicated).

maya: customer also complained about 400 errors labeled `dimension mismatch`. our runtime currently only validates shape at kernel selection time; we could add early validation to reject inconsistent dimension headers to fail fast (400) and avoid hitting expensive padding path. but note customer already got 400s in some cases which triggered retries.

sarah: for immediate mitigation we can:
- revert r23.4 batching heuristics to previous grouping (short-term rollback)
- set embed-pool-3 to conservative max_batch_size=256 and enable strict_dim_grouping for that pool
- rate-limit retries for organizations that get 400s to prevent thundering herd

jim: I can push rollback to canary region now and a full rollback if canary looks good.

billing-bot: flagged potential billing impact for SUP-4821: estimated extra GPU runtime ~+68% for 17:09-17:30 window. recommend issuing credit if rollback doesn't fully mitigate.

maya: timeline we agreed on in thread:
- T+15m: canary rollback of batching heuristics (jim)
- T+30m: backfill strict-dimension validation for embed endpoints (elias)
- T+1h: revert embed-pool config and confirm vectors/sec recovery (sarah)
- T+2h: follow-up with customer + propose billing credit (maya, billing)

elias: quick patch sketch (pseudo) to add server-side strict check:

```python
# in embeddings request path
client_dim = request.headers.get('X-Client-Dimensions')
model_dim = model_metadata[model].embedding_dim
if client_dim and int(client_dim) != model_dim:
    return Response(400, json={'error':'dimension mismatch', 'expected': model_dim})
```

maya: customer is on standby for rollback. they can flip to backup endpoint we provided if needed.

diego: notes for postmortem/upstream fixes:
- add unit tests for mixed-dimension batching and ensure kernel selection not forced to fallback path incorrectly
- add metric `batch_padding_rate` and alert when >5% for embedding pools
- clarify docs and SDK: avoid sending dimension headers; include strict-dim flag in SDKs
- add throttling for automatic retries on 400 responses to avoid amplifying incidents

sarah: update: T+12m after canary rollback, embed-pool-3 gpu_util steady ~45% and vectors/sec for org recovered from 28k->105k. queue_depth back to normal.

maya: customer verified improvement and paused escalation. billing team: please prepare credit proposal.

billing-bot: proposal drafted, will attach to ticket SUP-4821.

elias: scheduling fix for strict-dim early rejection and tests into sprint. will also add regression test that simulates mixed-dim clients with new batcher heuristics.

maya: closing loop once billing/PRs merged. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
